summary: build-viability is rejected for the fifth round running. Round 5 genuinely removed the four synthetic constants and genuinely extracted crossCheckVerdict(), and its six ungrounded requirement tokens and twelve ungrounded ladder flags are real findings that I verified independently. But the class it claims to have removed survives everywhere a COUNT was substituted for a CHECK. I broke the model detector three new ways, the strongest of which resurrects round 3's exact defect: freezing the RI-CHR02 matrix race argument for every giver leaves the 12x10 matrix 100% dead, and --verify-model still reports RACE-SENSITIVE / 4-of-4 anchors AGREE / exit 0, because ONE giver still moves through a second, unmodelled race channel (fDispRaceMod). The full walk on that tree publishes instead of refusing. The advertised grant-dependency guard fires 0 times in 540 rows and is dead code; all 495 abstentions come from criterionThreeFactionsRank5, which abstains on a pure counting argument and never re-runs the compatibility search, so a shadow tree where no three factions can EVER coexist produces output byte-identical to the sound tree. And the self-test, run to completion for the first time, is RED on two checks, one of which is the falsification control for criterion 2 refusing to go red; its own final line reads: build-viability self-test: FAIL (49/51).
worst_instrument_why: Fifth round running. The round's own best lesson — a field census over data cannot prove a read dead, because the loader defines what shapes are legal — was written down and then not applied to its own producer branch, its own grant ledger, its own abstention path or its own model detector. In each case a count stands in for a check: 15 ledger rows counted rather than classified (substitutions_remaining is a filter over a hand-written literal that no code ever labels), factions counted rather than tested for compatibility (line 2044), and gated givers counted as moved without asking WHICH race term moved them (race_sensitive: moved.length > 0, line 3226).
broke_the_model_detector_how: Three distinct one-or-two-line breaks on shadow trees at 0b2d6ef, none of them R3's known one-liner (which I ran as my red control and which the tool does catch, exit 20). D3: freeze the matrix race argument for every giver — matrix 100% dead, detector says RACE-SENSITIVE 1/31, AGREES, exit 0, VALID attestation written, and the full walk publishes 0/540 viable / 45 not viable / 495 UNMEASURABLE identical to the sound tree. D2: swap dunmer<->nord — output identical to the sound control on every reported field, only source_hash differs; 12/12 recorded givers have their arms exactly swapped. D1: freeze the race for 30 of 31 givers — detector says RACE-SENSITIVE 2/31 (sound: 25/31) and the MIXED warning does not even fire.

findings: DEFECT F (headline). shadowD3 freezes the RI-CHR02 matrix race argument for EVERY giver (`race: __matrixRace` with __matrixRace='dunmer') and leaves _questPlayerView() untouched. --verify-model reports RACE-SENSITIVE (1/31 gated givers moved), '31 modelled, 0 unmodelled', 4/4 anchors AGREES, exit 0, and writes a VALID attestation. The full walk then PUBLISHES 0/540 viable, 45 not viable, 495 UNMEASURABLE — byte-identical to the sound tree — instead of refusing. The builder's own acceptance test ('the full walk on that tree must REFUSE') fails.

WHY F WORKS: race reaches canOffer through TWO independent channels and `moved.length > 0` cannot attribute movement to either. (1) game/src/character/reaction.js raceTerm() — the RI-CHR02 12x10 matrix, which is what the tool models with dispositionCeiling(). (2) game/src/sim/dialogue/disposition.js:297 — `if (npc.race && player.race && npc.race === player.race) x += G.fDispRaceMod`, a flat same-race bonus via dlgMovableTerms. In D3 channel 1 is dead and channel 2 alone moves ONE giver (salt-factor-neloth-vaun, dunmer, delta -5).

DAMAGE F CERTIFIES AS SOUND, measured by my own Node-side probe importing the shipped raceTerm(): the matrix race term differs dunmer->nord for 25 of 31 gated givers, largest |delta| 24 (RG-DEEP -40 -> -16). That 25/31 independently reproduces shadowS's LIVE 25/31 without booting anything.

DEFECT G. shadowD2 swaps dunmer<->nord before the matrix read. Output identical to the sound control on every reported field (RACE-SENSITIVE 25/31, 31 modelled 0 unmodelled, 4/4 AGREES, exit 0); only source_hash differs. 12/12 recorded givers have arms exactly swapped (dyer-sallis: sound dunmer 9/nord 31, D2 dunmer 31/nord 9). A race term wired backwards is indistinguishable from a correct one.

DEFECT H. shadowD1 freezes the matrix race for 30 of 31 givers. Detector: RACE-SENSITIVE 2/31 (sound 25/31), '31 modelled, 0 unmodelled' — the MIXED warning does NOT fire, because `modelled` reports only that the closure returned an object, not that the race term inside it did anything. AGREES, exit 0. race_sensitive: moved.length > 0 (:3226) is a threshold of one.

DEFECT A. `substitutions_remaining` is rows.filter(r => r.basis === 'SUBSTITUTION').length over a HAND-WRITTEN literal array (:1432-1449). No row is ever labelled 'SUBSTITUTION'. The count is 0 by construction; --self-test asserts it to 0, asserting a tautology. The ledger's own doc comment at :1422 defines player-optimal-bound as 'THE ONE SURVIVING SUBSTITUTION, stated as one', so the file says there are four and reports zero.

DEFECT B. REPUTATION is not a player-optimal bound but a JOINTLY UNREACHABLE vector. REPUTATION_GIFTS (:1379-1398) takes the max delta PER FACTION INDEPENDENTLY across resolutions and drops every negative. Measured on 121 quests: 64 have their per-faction maxima coming from different, mutually exclusive resolutions; 200 negative deltas summing -3443 are discarded. Q-ASSZ-04 credits imperial_assize +42, xul_aneekh +25 and drowned_court +20 from ONE quest. A real one-resolution-per-quest play optimising the_dockhands reaches dockhands 521 but house_dres -236; the tool holds dockhands 521 AND house_dres 169 simultaneously.

DEFECT I. The grant-dependency test is DEAD CODE: 0 of 540. I patched a probe copy adding a THIRD arm granting only the quest's own ungrounded tokens instead of full omniscience, and tallied over --signatures all: 'hatch taken 0 times: ATTRIBUTED 0, LAUNDERED 0'. The advertised anti-substitution guard never executes on this tree and cannot be credited. It is also unsound in shape — omniscient:true grants all five collections and the flip is blamed on whichever tokens the quest carries, with nothing checking causation — but that is latent only because the path is dead.

DEFECT J. All 495 abstentions come from criterionThreeFactionsRank5, which abstains on a pure COUNTING argument (:2044-2045, `qualifying.length + blockedOnlyByAnUngroundedFlag.length >= 3`) and NEVER re-runs the compatibility search over qualifying + blocked. DEMONSTRATED: shadowE rewrites exclusivity.enemy_pairs into 12 pairs making the compatibility graph bipartite K4,4 and therefore triangle-free; my independent probe using the shipping FactionGates confirms 0 mutually compatible triples with ALL 8 ladders granted rank 5. The tool still reports three_factions_rank5 unmeasurable x540 and prints 'held back ONLY by a rank-5 world_state flag', output byte-identical to the sound tree. A total, data-irreparable build failure laundered into an abstention.

DEFECT C (still live, and grown). PRODUCERS' npcs/** branch is `for (const g of Object.values(d)) if (g && Array.isArray(g.npcs))` — a nested-group shape. At 0b2d6ef game/data/npcs has 15 files, ALL with top-level doc.npcs (what loadNPCs() reads), 0 nested: 347 records and 776 topics under the loader shape, 0 collected by the tool's branch. The grant ledger cites 'npcs[].topics' as a source contributing nothing. The builder's sweep recorded 'npc record fields ... topics 336/336' — a FIELD census — while its own code path reached 0 of those records. Impact measured honestly: exactly one shipped gate names a topic produced only by an npc record (Q-LILM-01.opens_by.prerequisite_topics[0] = 'the rotting quarter'); repairing the branch moves GRANTED_TOPICS 226 -> 227 and no verdict moves, because the dialogue layer separately produces the slug. Dead, cited, and currently harmless — a false red waiting for a topic only an NPC teaches.

DEFECT D (carried, re-confirmed at 0b2d6ef). `viable` is 0 BY CONSTRUCTION: criterionThreeFactionsRank5 is UNMEASURABLE for 540 of 540 signatures, and evaluateSignature sets viable only when all four criteria PASS. No signature on this tree can be viable whatever the build does. The headline '0 of 540 viable (target 486)' is a number the instrument's shape guarantees — the same class as round 4's 0 of 540 from reputation=100, reached from the restrictive side instead of the permissive one. The tool's own falsification control for this criterion now confirms it (self-test failure 2).

TWO SURVIVING CROSS-CHECK TAUTOLOGIES. (a) pairs_enumerated is DEFINED as comparedRows.length + unresolvedRows.length (:3309), so accounting_holds (:3332) is identically true and can never fail; the self-test asserts it. (b) the loop at :3412 does `if (engineValue === undefined) continue;`, dropping pairs into NEITHER array, so the why string's claim that N pairs were enumerated under-reports the real enumeration.

ACCEPTED, and it is real work: the four synthetic constants are genuinely gone (gold summed from real rewards[], ranks from the shipping FactionGates.highestQualifying(), the four collections real Sets that refuse an unproduced token); crossCheckVerdict() is genuinely extracted, the compared array's length is genuinely the count, and a row without a boolean `agrees` genuinely refuses; --verify-model is a genuine advance over source-text anchors and does catch R3's break.

DEFECT L (successor pass, angle 1 — a substitution wearing a derivation that the ledger does not classify as either). `worldFlags` is labelled derived-from-data, value 770, and is NOT in the declared-bounds list — but it is built exactly like `reputation`, which IS declared a player-optimal-bound: the union of what EVERY resolution of EVERY quest produces, with no choice ever made. Measured on the shipped book at 88ee56d: 755 flags produced anywhere; 91 of 124 quests have >1 mutually exclusive resolution each producing world flags; 601 of 755 flags are CONTESTED (every producer is one branch of a branching quest) and only 154 uncontested. The granted set is not merely optimistic but self-contradictory — Q-SAP-01 contributes ixtu_vakh_trusts_player AND ixtu_vakh_closed_to_player, and sap_route_to_archon_open AND sap_route_to_archon_closed; Q-ARCH-01 contributes archon_vats_open AND archon_vats_burned. This propagates: worldFlags is the INPUT to the `ranks` row, the one labelled shipping-predicate and defended as 'the same call QuestEngine.context() makes'. That defence is true of the predicate and false of the argument; a shipped predicate evaluated against a world state no player can occupy is not a shipping-predicate measurement, and the label as printed launders it.

DEFECT L impact, measured honestly and currently NIL. World flags are read by exactly one kind of gate: the 24 faction-ladder world_state.flag rows. NO quest gate demands a world flag at all — the complete set of resolution requirement keys is attributes/condition/disposition/faction_rank/gold/items/knowledge/skills/spell_effects, and opens_by offers only overheard_from/prerequisite_quests/prerequisite_topics/topic. Of the 24 ladder demands, 12 are ungrounded and the 12 grounded ones are all UNCONTESTED — each is produced by every resolution of its quest, so it is reachable whichever branch the player picks. I checked this expecting a collision and did not find one; reported as the negative result it is. So DEFECT L is the same species as DEFECT C: real, undeclared, currently harmless — a false green waiting for the first contested-flag prerequisite.

DEFECT A restated from the tool's own stdout at 88ee56d, starker than the :1422 doc comment the predecessor cited: --audit-grants contradicts itself in THREE CONSECUTIVE PRINTED LINES. The `completed` row's caveat reads '... stated because it is a substitution and it must be visible'; two lines later 'substitutions remaining: 0'; one line after that 'player-optimal bounds (declared, not hidden): reputation, gold, completed, locked'. A row that calls itself a substitution, four declared bounds, and a counter reporting zero — on the mode the help text calls 'the mode to run first'.
MINOR (successor pass): reports/viability.json carries "unmeasurable": 495 beside "unmeasurable_because": [] — the field that exists to explain the abstentions is empty on every run.
rebuild: Model detector must measure the MODELLED term, not movement: per gated giver assert explainDisposition(id).race_term under both races equals the shipped raceTerm(chData, group, race, upbringing).race, by value and by sign. That is a 31-row equality check against an already-exposed field and it kills D1, D2 and D3 at once. Name and measure the second race channel (fDispRaceMod) separately.

Delete substitutions_remaining or make it derivable. A count over a hand-written literal is not an audit: classify each row by a rule the code applies, or state the four surviving player-optimal bounds as the four substitutions the file already calls them.

Reputation must be a REACHABLE vector: one resolution per quest, negatives carried, bound reported under a single consistent playthrough. If the tool will not solve that, it must report reputation as an upper bound that is NOT jointly attainable and refuse any verdict turning on two factions at once.
Apply the grant-dependency flip test at :2044 — grant the ungrounded flags, re-run the triple search, abstain only on an ACTUAL flip; otherwise FAIL.
Attribute the quest-level hatch too (grant only the quest's own ungrounded tokens, not full omniscience) and report that it fires 0 times, so a reader knows it is untested by the tree.
Fix the npcs/** producer branch to the loader's top-level doc.npcs shape, and re-run the whole sweep against LOADERS rather than field censuses.

Green the self-test. Give the seed ladder a partial-saturation guard naming the residual non-disposition stop (Q-XULA-06, the_xul_aneekh rank 4/5) the way :2846 already does for total saturation, and make criterion 2's falsification control able to go red.
Put `0 of 540 viable` in context on the front page: it is guaranteed by criterion 2 being unmeasurable for every signature and must not read as a build verdict.
Remove the two cross-check tautologies (accounting_holds, pairs_enumerated) and count the `engineValue === undefined` pairs into a third named bucket.

Declare worldFlags as the fifth bound, or make it reachable (DEFECT L). 601 of 755 produced flags are contested and the granted set holds directly contradictory pairs. Either pick one resolution per quest and grant only what that play yields, or label the row player-optimal-bound and stop calling the `ranks` row a shipping-predicate measurement when its argument is an impossible world. Also fill unmeasurable_because, which is [] on every run.
